message.content:
I recently picked up a used mechanical keyboard from an online marketplace for thirty-eight dollars, hoping to save some cash while upgrading my home office setup. The listing claimed it was in “good condition,” but the reality was a bit more complicated. My first major red flag appeared during the pre-purchase inquiry phase; I asked the seller specifically about the switch type, and it took a full week to receive a vague response. That level of communication certainly set a concerning tone before the item even arrived.

Upon unboxing, the issues became immediately apparent. The spacebar has a persistent, annoying rattle every time I hit it, which sounds like loose stabilizers or perhaps just general wear and tear. Additionally, the ‘E’ key occasionally double-types, forcing me to backspace more often than I would like. Despite these mechanical flaws, I have surprisingly decided to keep it. Why? Because the keycaps are incredibly smooth, and the overall typing experience remains comfortable for long sessions. I spend hours drafting detailed emails daily, and my wrists feel significantly less strained compared to my old membrane keyboard. Given the low price point and the hassle of repackaging and shipping it back, I figured I could live with the quirks. It is not perfect, but for thirty-eight dollars, it serves its purpose adequately enough for my daily writing tasks, even if the rattling spacebar drives me slightly crazy.
